'''''Salvia argentea''''', the '''silver sage''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SAAR25|taxon=Salvia argentea|access-date=28 October 2015}}</ref> '''silver salvia''', or '''silver clary''', is a biennial or short-lived [[perennial plant]] that is native to an area in southern Europe from [[Portugal]] to [[Bulgaria]]. Its Latin [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''argentea'' means "silvery", referring to the colour of the leaves.<ref name="Clebsch">{{cite book|last1=Clebsch|first1=Betsy|last2=Barner|first2=Carol D.|title=The New Book of Salvias|publisher=Timber Press|year=2003|pages=36–37|isbn=978-0-88192-560-9|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NM0iwB8GrQYC&pg=PA36}}</ref>

==Description==
''Salvia argentea'' has a large spread of basal leaves that measure {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} wide and {{convert|30|to|60|cm|ft|abbr=on}} high. The individual leaves are {{convert|20|to|30|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and  {{convert|15|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide. Both leaf surfaces are heavily covered with silky hairs that give it a wooly appearance. The leaves are soft to the touch, first emerging as a distinctive silvery white and then turning to grey-green after flowering. Cool weather in the [[autumn]] turns the leaves silvery again.<ref name="Clebsch" />

Flowers appear in spring or summer on {{convert|60|to|90|cm|in|abbr=on}} candelabra-like stalks that rise well above the foliage. The inconspicuous white flowers are tinged with yellow or pink. Cutting the flowers before they set seed results in a long-lived plant.<ref name="Clebsch" />

''Salvia argentea'' has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16310/Salvia-argentea/Details | title = ''Salvia argentea'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> It requires a south-facing position in full sun. Although hardy down to {{convert|-15|C|F|abbr=on}} it dislikes the combination of winter wet and freezing temperatures. It may therefore be short-lived.
